ruleset.name: Explicitness Rules
ruleset.description: The Explicitness Ruleset finds implicit inputs and outputs, as defined in "Grokking Simplicity" by Eric Normand. A method's explicit inputs are its arguments and its explicit output is its return value. Any other way that data enters or leaves the method is implicit, and makes the method an action rather than a calculation. It is opt-in and is not part of the csharp ruleset.

rule.name: ImplicitInput
rule.description: Data enters the method other than through its arguments. This rule flags: reads of the class's own mutable static fields and static auto-properties (constants and static readonly fields are fixed, so they are not inputs); the clock (DateTime.Now, Stopwatch), the environment, console input, file and directory reads, Guid.NewGuid() and unseeded random numbers. Pass the value in as an argument instead. Static constructors are exempt.

rule.name: ImplicitOutput
rule.description: Data leaves the method other than through its return value. This rule flags: writes to the class's own static state and changes to the objects that it holds; changes to an argument's object (member or element writes, and calls whose result is discarded, such as list.Add(x)); writes to ref and out parameters; console, debug and trace output; file and directory writes; environment changes, process exit and process start. Return the new value instead. Assigning a new value to a by-value parameter stays in the method, so it is not flagged. Static constructors are exempt.
